issues.failure_explanation: To derive (s2.78) the proof divides the identity (lambda_h-lambda)(u_h,v_h) = [residual expression] by (u_h,v_h) and asserts a uniform positive lower bound on |(u_h,v_h)| for v_h = u_h^* or I_h u^*. As h->0 this tends to (u,u^*), which vanishes exactly when lambda is defective. For an ascent-2 defective eigenvalue with converging eigenpairs one has |lambda-lambda_h| ~ h^s while the right-hand side of (s2.78) is O(h^{2s}), so (s2.78) fails. Neither lem3-7 (stated for an arbitrary jth eigenpair, in a framework that explicitly enumerates multiple/cluster eigenvalues) nor th3-8 (whose only hypothesis is 'the conditions of Theorem th3-1') assumes lambda non-defective.

failure_location.quote: Applying the same argument as in Lemma 5 in \cite{Wang2024}, we deduce that $|(\mathbf{u}_{h},\mathbf{v}_{h})|$ has a positive lower bound uniformly with respect to $h$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to lem3-7 and to th3-8 the assumption that lambda is non-defective (equivalently (u,u^*) != 0 for the chosen eigenfunction and adjoint eigenfunction); the cited lower-bound argument then applies.
issues.overall_effect: Estimate (s2.78) is unsupported and can fail for defective eigenvalues; the eigenvalue a posteriori reliability (s3.33) inherits the same hypothesis gap. The a priori estimates (s2.81)-(s2.85) and Corollary cor:added-1 already assume non-defectiveness and are unaffected.
issues.title: Eigenvalue duality estimate (s2.78) used without the non-defectiveness hypothesis needed for the uniform lower bound on (u_h,v_h)
issues.why_classification: The statements are false as written for defective eigenvalues, a regime the paper explicitly develops cluster machinery for; the repair is a limited weakening (an added hypothesis on the eigenvalue class) that leaves recognizably comparable results, and all advertised claims (formulated for non-defective clusters) survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The second equality in (s2.88) inserts I_h T^*u_i^* via Galerkin orthogonality. The only orthogonality available for A_h(e, w_h) with e=(T-T_h)u_j is the primal one for data u_j ((s2.26) minus (s2.41)): A_h(e,w_h) = -B_h(w_h, S u_j - S_h u_j). Hence the middle term must be B_h(T^*u_i^* - I_hT^*u_i^*, S u_j - S_h u_j), not B_h(T^*u_i^* - I_hT^*u_i^*, S^*u_i^* - S_h^*u_i^*) as printed; the difference B_h(I_hT^*u_i^*, (S^*u_i^* - S_h^*u_i^*) - (S u_j - S_h u_j)) does not vanish in general, so the equality is false as written. (The first line's T^*u_j^* is also a misprint for T^*u_i^*.) The final bound |((T-T_h)u_j, u_i^*)| <~ h^{2s} still holds because both pressure errors are O(h^s).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the middle term by B_h(T^*u_i^* - I_hT^*u_i^*, S u_j - S_h u_j); the rest of the estimate is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: One false equality inside the proof of (s2.80); the statement of (s2.80) and all downstream results remain valid once the term is corrected.
issues.title: Wrong pressure-error factor in the duality expansion (s2.88)
issues.why_classification: A single-term correction in one displayed identity; the conclusion and every dependent result survive, so it is a short local repair with no mathematical loss.

issues.failure_explanation: From (s2.78) with [v_h,q_h]=[I_h u^*, vartheta_h p^*], the residuals A_h(u-u_h, u^*-I_h u^*) and B_h(u-u_h, p^*-vartheta_h p^*) can only be bounded through the energy norm |||u-u_h||| (times h^r||u^*||_{1+r}), giving |lambda-lambda_h| <~ h^r(|||u-u_h||| + ||p-p_h||_0) up to higher-order terms. The printed (s2.90) asserts the stronger bound with h^r||u-u_h||_0; since generically |||u-u_h||| ~ h^s while ||u-u_h||_0 ~ h^{r+s}, the printed inequality is not derivable from (s2.78) and fails whenever the pressure error is anomalously small relative to the velocity energy error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ||u-u_h||_0 by |||u-u_h||| in (s2.90); the subsequent absorption proving (s2.91) is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: A displayed intermediate claim in the proof of th2-7 is not derivable as written. The theorem's conclusions (s2.81)-(s2.85) survive, because the absorption argument leading to (s2.91) works identically with the corrected energy-norm version.
issues.title: Intermediate eigenvalue estimate (s2.90) uses the L2 norm of the velocity error where the proof only yields the energy norm
issues.why_classification: A forced, local norm correction in one intermediate inequality; no conclusion, rate, or downstream result is affected.

issues.failure_explanation: The face-bubble derivation (s3.30) contains the convective term int_F [⁅(u_h-u)⊗beta⁆]·Theta_bar ds, which is bounded by ||beta||_infty ||[⁅u-u_h⁆ ]||_{0,F} ||Theta||_{0,F} with ||Theta||_{0,F} <~ h_F||R||_{0,F}. After Young's inequality and a trace inequality this contributes a term of order ||u-u_h||_{0,omega(F)} (scaling like h^{1/2}||[⁅u-u_h⁆ ]||_{0,F}) to eta_{F_tau}, which is absent from the printed right-hand sides of (s3.25) and (s3.28). A discrete solution with a large jump across F but small elementwise gradients makes eta_{F_tau} of order ||u-u_h||_{0,omega} while the printed bound (only ||nabla(u-u_h)|| and ||p-p_h|| plus higher-order terms) stays small, so the inequalities fail as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add ||u-u_h||_{0,omega(tau)} (respectively ||u^*-u_h^*||_{0,omega(tau)}) to the right-hand sides of (s3.25) and (s3.28); the proof of th3-6 then goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The local efficiency inequalities for eta_{F_tau} and eta^*_{F_tau} are false as written. The global efficiency result th3-6 survives, because the missing term sums to ||u-u_h||_0^2 <= ||u-u_h||_h^2.
issues.title: Local efficiency bounds (s3.25) and (s3.28) omit the L2 error contribution of the convective flux jump
issues.why_classification: A local one-term addition repairs the estimates and leaves the global efficiency theorem and all later claims intact, with no new argument needed beyond the standard trace/Young steps.

issues.failure_explanation: Bounding the residual products of (s2.78) via (s2.16)-(s2.17), (s2.65)-(s2.66) and the reliability estimates (s3.22)-(s3.23) necessarily produces, besides the printed terms, ||lambda u - lambda_h u_h||_0^2, ||lambda^* u^* - lambda_h^* u_h^*||_0^2 and cross terms such as eta_h ||lambda^* u^* - lambda_h^* u_h^*||_0. These cannot be dominated by the printed right-hand side of (s3.33) from within the a posteriori theory alone: eliminating them requires the a priori estimates (s2.81)-(s2.85) together with an absorption of C|lambda-lambda_h|^2 for h sufficiently small, an argument that is nowhere given (and that itself needs the non-defectiveness hypothesis of ISSUE-001).

failure_location.quote:
Choosing  $ [\mathbf{v}_{h},q_{h}]=
[\mathbf{u}_{h}^{*},p_{h}^{*}]$ in (\ref{s2.78}), from (\ref{s2.16}),  (\ref{s2.17}), (\ref{s2.65}),  (\ref{s2.66}), (\ref{s3.22}) and (\ref{s3.23}), we obtain (\ref{s3.33}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Append ||lambda u - lambda_h u_h||_0^2 + ||lambda^* u^* - lambda_h^* u_h^*||_0^2 (and cross terms) to (s3.33), or add the absorption argument using (s2.81)-(s2.85) with an explicit 'for h sufficiently small' qualifier and the non-defectiveness assumption.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem th3-8's inequality is unsupported as stated; it is valid only for h sufficiently small after a missing absorption argument, or with the higher-order terms appended (the phrasing 'up to the oscillation terms' in Corollary cor:added-1 suggests the intended reading). The cluster corollary and the adaptive algorithm's theoretical basis survive with that qualification.
issues.title: Eigenvalue a posteriori bound (s3.33) silently drops the higher-order eigen-error terms; no absorption argument is given
issues.why_classification: The proof does not establish the stated inequality; closing the gap needs a contained but nontrivial absorption argument plus a small-h qualifier (or a limited weakening of the statement by higher-order terms), while no new global proof architecture or major loss results.
